g.textArea: CTO / team | Draft | Bring DevOps code together while keeping ownership and execution boundaries clear.
Blue = proposed | Gray = saved evidence or context | Yellow = tradeoff, exception or team decision
Current: separate repositories in saved evidence
Proposed: one DevOps repository, distinct areas

rect.data-content:
Terraform
tl-trekai-terraform: TL and shared infrastructure
tl-trekcap-terraform: CAP RD infrastructure

GitOps
tl-lms-gitOps: dev, stage, prod and common
cap-gitOps: RD configuration

Other infrastructure candidates
ir-terraform-temporary; b-metric-dashboard-terraform
Legacy trekai-infra: review before including

Scope to confirm
Locate Ansible, scripts and other DevOps-owned code.
devops/ Proposed repository name; team to agree

terraform/
Keep product, environment and state boundaries explicit.

gitops/
Separate TL and CAP configuration and environment paths.

automation/
Ansible if used, plus reviewed DevOps scripts.

.github/ and docs/
Shared validation, ownership rules and operating guidance.

• Easier discovery and consistent structure.
• Reuse checks and operating guidance.
• Review related configuration changes together.

• More complex dependency-aware validation.
• Wider impact from shared workflow changes.
• Recheck repository access and integrations.

Keep repositories separate with shared workflows
and standards. Compare access needs, team effort
and coordination cost before choosing.

Team decision
Agree repository scope, owners and access before migration. Folder review rules do not isolate read access.
If code requires separate visibility, keep that scope in a separate repository. Shared state and release scope remain separate decisions.

g.textArea: Evidence: saved GitHub inventory Nov 3 and Terraform/GitOps evidence Nov 3–4, 2026. Repository names and folders are snapshot observations, not a live inventory.
Contributors / reviewers / DevOps | Draft | One place to propose changes; execution stays specific to each affected area.
Blue = proposed | Gray = saved evidence or context | Yellow = tradeoff, exception or team decision

rect.data-content:
1. Open a pull request
Change the relevant area.
Describe intent and affected targets.

2. Check affected scope
Detect paths and dependencies.
Run the relevant validation.

3. Review the change
Owners inspect results and impact.
All affected areas get review.

4. Merge agreed code
Required checks and reviews pass.
Route each change to its process.

Checks fail or scope is unclear
Block merge; return diagnostics.
Author revises and reruns checks.

Changes requested
Author revises the pull request.
Repeat checks and affected review.

Terraform changes
Final target plan and authorization.
Apply and verify under Proposal 01.
Keep each state independent.

GitOps changes
Argo CD reads approved paths.
Reconcile under agreed policy.
Verify the deployment outcome.

Other automation
Use its agreed trigger, identity and authorization.
Include run results in the change record.

What validation needs to understand
Terraform: validate affected roots and shared-module consumers; show target plans.
GitOps: validate affected manifests, charts and values, including shared dependencies.
Scripts / Ansible: choose suitable checks after inventory; unclear impact blocks merge.

Ownership and access
Route reviews to each affected area. Restrict execution identities by target.
A shared commit can coordinate code; it does not make separate deployments atomic.

Agree with the team: required reviewers and checks; dependency detection; cross-area ordering; who handles failures.
App build writers and Argo CD references need an explicit migration plan. Broader release-policy redesign belongs to Proposal 11.

g.textArea: Proposed workflow. Saved evidence shows app workflows write GitOps changes; Terraform apply and Argo CD reconciliation are separate. Current execution and access remain unverified.
DevOps / team | Draft | Confirm the boundaries, prove a small migration, then move one agreed scope at a time.
Blue = proposed | Gray = saved evidence or context | Yellow = tradeoff, exception or team decision

rect.data-content:
1. Understand today’s setup
List candidate code, owners and consumers.
Map workflows, access, state references
and Argo CD sources before moving files.

2. Agree the repository boundaries
Compare consolidation with shared standards.
Choose scope, folders and ownership.
Agree access, checks and migration criteria.

3. Prove a small migration
Move one agreed development scope.
Check review, automation and references.
Rehearse cutover and rollback.

4. Move the rest step by step
Switch one source of truth per scope.
Verify consumers after every cutover.
Retire old write paths after acceptance.

• Show checks for changed files and shared dependencies.
• Demonstrate required reviews and scoped execution.
• Prove app writers and Argo CD use the new locations.
• Confirm Terraform resolves the same intended state.

• Inventory every writer and reader before the switch.
• Freeze the migrating scope; update references together.
• Keep one writable source of truth after cutover.
• Rehearse restoring consumers and reconciling changes.

• Argo CD repository, revision and path references.
• App workflow targets and GitHub App repository access.
• Terraform paths, module sources and backend settings.
• Approval rules, identity bindings, docs and runbooks.

• Confirm Ansible, scripts, business and legacy scope.
• Agree naming, history handling and area owners.
• Retain separate repos where access needs require it.
• Choose the pilot, rollback owner and acceptance criteria.

Keep the proposal boundaries clear
Proposal 01 covers controlled Terraform execution. Proposals 03/04 cover application monorepos. Proposal 11 covers GitOps / SDLC simplification.
Repository consolidation alone does not resolve release policy, access or recovery gaps. No migration dates or named owners are committed.

g.textArea: Planning basis: saved infrastructure / GitOps map and control assessment, Nov 3–6, 2026. Migration and runtime verification are proposed work, not completed actions.
